first_impression.reaction: I googled 'santorini wedding' because it keeps coming up when we talk about Greece. The intro assumes we've already picked it ('Santorini is the choice, or very nearly'), which we haven't, but the next line is the useful bit: legal or symbolic, season, setting, guest list, travel, documents, house rules, weekend, in that order. No 'say I do in paradise', just a plan. That's enough to keep me reading.

journey.quote: Take them in that order and each one narrows the next.
journey.reaction: Good. That's what I want from a planner: tell us what to decide first so we're not doing spreadsheets for 18 months.

journey.section: Step 1: Decide between a legal and a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: A symbolic ceremony on the island, after a legal step at home, keeps the paperwork in Australia and frees the day itself.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, said without making the symbolic route sound second best. I'm a lawyer, and I already suspect this is what we'll do.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but it may not work as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. Exactly the kind of thing that bites you six months later at the bank.

journey.section: Step 2: Weather by month from official station data
journey.quote: The figures below are for Naxos, the nearest official station, so read them as a guide to the neighbourhood rather than a forecast for the caldera.
journey.reaction: I like that they admit the numbers aren't from Santorini rather than pretending. James will like the table. My takeaway: May or September, not October.

journey.section: Step 2: Heat, wind and wildfire advice for travellers
journey.quote: Neither is a reason to look elsewhere, but both are reasons to keep travel insurance in place for everyone travelling.
journey.reaction: Calm and straight. This whole block is going to Mum and Dad, who will absolutely ask about the volcano.

journey.quote: Its terraces look out over the caldera, a setting made for vows at sunset.
journey.reaction: Bit brochure-y. Everything around it is specific and this line slides into the 'dream sunset' language every other site uses.

journey.section: Step 4: Size your guest list against capacity and rooms
journey.quote: The caldera-edge spaces in Oia and Imerovigli seat between 15 and 60.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful sentence in the piece for us. At 60 to 90 guests, the postcard terraces mostly don't fit, and the table shows it plainly. Venetsanos at about 100 seated is the one I'd look at. Nobody else has told me this so bluntly.

journey.section: Step 5: Plan travel for your guests
journey.quote: Guests flying from Australia arrive tired, and some will be older or less steady on stairs.
journey.reaction: That's Nan, exactly. And the step-free route questions are the ones I'd never have thought to ask until we were standing at the top of 200 steps.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness.
journey.reaction: By here I'm skimming. If we sign at home, I don't think most of Step 6 applies to us, but I had to read a fair way in to be sure.

journey.section: Step 7: Lock in the house rules in writing
journey.quote: Grace Hotel requires a wedding planner for every wedding, involved for at least 3 months beforehand, and gives you a dedicated event manager for the venue itself.
journey.reaction: Useful, and it's the sort of thing only someone who reads the contracts knows. Answers part of my 'what does end-to-end actually mean' question: the venue's person is not our person.

journey.section: Step 7: Lock in the house rules in writing
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Yes. This plus the Step 9 checklist goes into our shared doc tonight.

journey.section: Plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: Calm, not pushy, and 'one person' is what I want. But I'd already read nearly the same line after Step 3, so the second time it sounds a bit scripted.

unanswered_questions: Is there a real Santorini wedding you've planned, with the venue and date, that we can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests, which setting would you actually steer us towards: one larger terrace like Venetsanos, or splitting events across spaces?
Who is physically there on the day: our Wedded Advisor, or the venue's event manager?
Who gets older guests from the airport to the hotel: the venue, Wedded Concierge, or us?
How far ahead do caldera venues usually book out for a May or September date?

turn_offs_found.turn_off: Clichés: fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise
turn_offs_found.quote: Its terraces look out over the caldera, a setting made for vows at sunset.
turn_offs_found.why: It's the one line that reads like a venue brochure. The rest of the article earns trust with numbers and trade-offs, so a stock sunset phrase stands out and makes it sound like every other wedding site.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: Not pushy at all, but the same promises come back almost word for word in the closing section. Repeated, it reads like a script rather than a person, which makes me wonder how personal the service really is.

would_share_with: James (partner): the Step 4 capacity table and the Step 9 checklist, so we can see Santorini is tight for our numbers
Mum and Dad (contributing): the heat, wildfire and earthquake paragraph with the travel insurance line
Both sets of parents: the Step 5 access questions, for the grandparents

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right and I trust the advice, but we haven't settled on Santorini, and the capacity table has actually made me less sure it fits 80 people. I'd read another post or two and want to see one real wedding you've done before handing over our details.

top_3_changes: In Step 3, Wineries and estates, replace 'a setting made for vows at sunset' with something concrete about the Santo Wines terraces, so it doesn't read like brochure copy.
At the top of Step 6, add one line telling couples who sign at home that they can skip to Step 7, so symbolic couples don't wade through the legalisation detail.
Say the 'time zone, AUD, confirmed in writing' promise once, either after Step 3 or in the closing, not both.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests to explain sourcing or not-published items, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Real weddings, on-the-day presence and guest transfers are business details (deferred). Listed as unanswered questions only, not must-fix.

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'santorini wedding' during early destination research, about 14 months out, Santorini not yet chosen.
Read Steps 1 to 5, 7 and 9 closely; skimmed Step 6 documents and the weather table.
No prices appear by design, so the 'vague pricing' turn-off was not raised.
Stock-photo turn-off not assessed because image slots are placeholders.
Family details (grandparents, parents contributing) are persona colour, not brand facts.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
